newsitem.title: USA: U.S. warns against unconstitutional move in Turkey.
newsitem.headline: U.S. warns against unconstitutional move in Turkey.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, in an apparent warning to the Turkish military, said on Friday there should be no "extra-constitutional" changes in Turkey.
But Albright also said the United States strongly supported the continuation of a secular system in Turkey, the goal to which Turkish military leaders say they are attached.

Albright was speaking two days after a top Turkish general, Fevzi Turkeri, urged ordinary Turks to fight the danger of Islamic activism and said the army's role was to protect the country "by force of arms" from domestic and external threats.
"We obviously are watching and have been watching the situation very carefully," Albright told reporters before talks with Latvian Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs.
"We have made very clear that it is essential that Turkey continue in a secular, democratic way," she said.

"We have also made clear that it's very important that whatever issues are going on there, whatever discussions and whatever changes people are thinking about, that they have to be within a democratic context and with no extra-constitutional approach."
But Albright added: "We appreciate the way that Turkey has in fact been a secular democracy."
Turkey has an Islamic-led government under Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan. But the administration, riven by internal dissension, appears close to collapse.
